forms[0].when: Add -는 to any verb stem, whether it ends in a vowel or a consonant: 먹다 → 먹는, 마시다 → 마시는. → Add -는 to the verb stem, whether it ends in a vowel or a consonant: 먹다 → 먹는, 마시다 → 마시는. (Stems ending in ㄹ drop the ㄹ: 살다 → 사는. See the ㄹ-stem row below.)

fixes.before: The action is happening now or happens regularly. Add -는 to any verb stem, whether it ends in a vowel or a consonant: 먹다 → 먹는, 마시다 → 마시는.
fixes.after: The action is happening now or happens regularly. Add -는 to the verb stem, whether it ends in a vowel or a consonant: 먹다 → 먹는, 마시다 → 마시는. (Stems ending in ㄹ drop the ㄹ: 살다 → 사는. See the ㄹ-stem row below.)

fixes.before: Use this for any adjective describing a noun. It shows the current state, so there is no separate present form with -는. If the stem ends in a consonant, add -은 (작다 → 작은). If it ends in a vowel, add -ㄴ (크다 → 큰).
fixes.after: Use this for any adjective describing a noun. If the stem ends in a consonant, add -은 (작다 → 작은). If it ends in a vowel, add -ㄴ (크다 → 큰).

fixes.before: Words ending in 있다 or 없다 (맛있다, 재미없다, 있다, 없다) always take -는, even when they work like adjectives in English.
fixes.after: Words ending in 있다 or 없다 (맛있다, 재미없다, 있다, 없다) take -는 (not -은) to describe a noun in the present, even when they work like adjectives in English.

fixes.before: When the stem ends in ㄹ, the ㄹ drops before -는 and -ㄴ. With -ㄹ, the two ㄹ merge into one. Do not add 으. Verbs: 살다 → 사는 / 산 / 살, 만들다 → 만드는 / 만든 / 만들. The same rule applies to adjectives: 멀다 → 먼.
fixes.after: When the stem ends in ㄹ, the ㄹ drops before -는 and -ㄴ. With -ㄹ, the two ㄹ merge into one. Do not add 으. Verbs: 살다 → 사는 / 산 / 살, 만들다 → 만드는 / 만든 / 만들.

fixes.before: Learners will be able to choose and form the correct noun-modifying ending (-는, -(으)ㄴ, -(으)ㄹ) for verbs, adjectives, 있다/없다 words, ㄹ-stems, and ㅂ-irregular adjectives.
fixes.after: Learners will be able to form the correct noun-modifying ending (-는, -(으)ㄴ, -(으)ㄹ) for verbs, adjectives, and irregular stems.

fixes.before: Korean puts describing words before the noun. Which ending you use depends on two things: whether the word is a verb or an adjective, and the time of the action. Verbs take -는 (now), -(으)ㄴ (past), or -(으)ㄹ (future or planned). Adjectives take -(으)ㄴ. Words ending in 있다/없다 always take -는. ㄹ-stems drop their ㄹ, and most ㅂ-adjectives change ㅂ to 우.
fixes.after: Describing words go before the noun in Korean: verbs take -는 (now), -(으)ㄴ (past), or -(으)ㄹ (future), and adjectives take -(으)ㄴ. 있다/없다 words take -는, ㄹ-stems drop ㄹ, and most ㅂ-adjectives change ㅂ to 우.

fixes.problem: The English says "does / is doing", which covers both the habitual/regular meaning and the ongoing one. The Indonesian "yang sedang dilakukan" only keeps "is doing" and loses the habitual meaning that lines 5 and 35 say -는 covers.
fixes.fix: (kata benda) yang dilakukan / sedang dilakukan seseorang

fixes.problem: English says 'most ㅂ-adjectives change ㅂ to 우'. The Vietnamese says 'hầu hết tính từ ㅂ bất quy tắc' ('most ㅂ-irregular adjectives'), which changes the rule: it suggests some irregular ones don't change, when the exceptions are actually regular adjectives like 좁다.
fixes.fix: Trong tiếng Hàn, từ miêu tả đứng trước danh từ: động từ dùng -는 (hiện tại), -(으)ㄴ (quá khứ), hoặc -(으)ㄹ (tương lai), còn tính từ dùng -(으)ㄴ. Các từ 있다/없다 dùng -는, thân từ kết thúc bằng ㄹ thì lược bỏ ㄹ, và hầu hết tính từ có thân kết thúc bằng ㅂ thì đổi ㅂ thành 우.

fixes.problem: The English "most ㅂ-adjectives" means adjectives whose stem ends in ㅂ. The Korean says "대부분의 ㅂ 불규칙 형용사" ("most ㅂ-irregular adjectives"), which changes the rule: every ㅂ-irregular adjective changes ㅂ to 우, so "most" makes no sense. It also contradicts line 29, which says a few ㅂ-ending adjectives are regular (좁다 → 좁은).

manual.after: Dalam bahasa Korea, kata penjelas diletakkan sebelum kata benda: kata kerja + -는 (sekarang), -(으)ㄴ (lampau), -(으)ㄹ (akan datang); kata sifat + -(으)ㄴ. Kata 있다/없다 + -는, batang ㄹ kehilangan ㄹ, dan ㅂ pada kebanyakan kata sifat menjadi 우.
